scope: All 24 eligible Reviewed additions assigned to bounded batch b1.
methodology: Every assigned record was compared to the actual public maintainer advisory structured fields and description prose; no proof of concept or source code was executed.

API and HTML response originals remain local only. Public artifacts contain allowlisted fields, independently written observations, response hashes and selected public headers, never full descriptions, code, credits, private-report links or tracking metadata.

Literal package coordinates, affected and fixed strings and source timestamps are preserved independently. CVSS numeric scores are copied only when published, never computed. HTML missing timestamps are marked unobservable, not asserted null source values.
limitations: This is a delta review, not a fresh primary-source review of the full corpus.
GitHub unauthenticated API rate limits required HTML fallback; individual failed attempts and successful HTML evidence are separate.
No independent KEV or real-world exploitation verification was performed.
Source-level range conflicts do not imply a local dependency applicability verdict.

database.summary: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys

maintainer.summary: Removal of emSign root cerificate

observations: Maintainer fields and prose identify 2026.10.18 as the fix, while Reviewed structured fixed is 2026.10.19. Reviewed prose itself says .18 removed all emSign roots and .19 restored only unaffected roots. Both PyPI releases exist; checksum-verified wheel bundles confirm .18 has no emSign root labels and .19 has G1/C1/C3 but not the implicated ECC G3. Use .18 as the issue-specific first fix boundary, preserve Reviewed .19 raw, and do not mistake .19 restoration for reintroduction of the implicated root.

The Reviewed narrative recommends 2026.10.19 or later. An issue-specific first fix boundary is not a claim that .18 is the preferred current upgrade target. Root-label checks are corroboration, not an independent cryptographic audit of the CA incident.
The source says emSign roots were removed because intermediate keys were compromised; do not infer a specific company incident or observed MITM from that library advisory alone.
